- issue_comment created in `experiment-repo`#9 ("Positive control for Δ(log Q), SE-ratio summary and C5 reference rows (from story-repo review 4)") by `experiment-repo`  > Interim answer (items 2, 3 and the C2 check are done and delivered to paper-repo `dev`; the positive control (item 1) is running and is the only open part).
  > 
  > **SE ratio** (`results/se_ratio.csv`, 91 data sets; ratio = bootstrap SE / model-based Fisher SE; median over data sets per design):
  > 
  > | design | cluster bootstrap | comparison bootstrap | same-graph null (comparison) | design effect (cluster/comparison)^2 |
  > |---|---|---|---|---|
  > | crowd | 0.81 | 0.82 | 0.82 | 0.98 |
  > | expert (MT-Bench human) | 1.30 | 0.84 | 0.83 | 2.39 |
  > | LLM judge | 1.00 | 0.99 | 0.99 | 1.03 |
  > | sports | 1.05 | 1.04 | 1.04 | 1.00 |
  > 
  > Real/null comparison-bootstrap ratio over all 91 sets: median 0.999, range 0.88-1.16. The raw crowd ratio below 1 is a tie effect the null shares (the model-based SE ignores that ties carry less variance), not a design effect. The one design effect is MT-Bench human: question clustering inflates the SE by about 1.55x. Sports is 1.00 by construction (one game per cluster). Use `real_over_null_cmp` and `design_effect_cluster` for the Table 2 column.
  > 
  > **C5 reference rows** (`predictive_rule.csv`, held-out RMSE of log k*, leave-one-data-set-out, 90 units; `mtbench_gpt4` has no first-order or null reference and is out of the comparison):
  > 
  > | predictor | delete | flip |
  > |---|---|---|
  > | fitted rule (base model) | 0.262 | 0.217 |
  > | null mean at matched z | 0.260 | 0.243 |
  > | first-order k rescaled by its median bias | 0.376 | 0.155 |
  > | log z only | about 0.44 | |
  > | intercept only | 0.81-0.85 | |
  > 
  > For flip the rescaled first-order prediction beats the regression (difference in squared error -0.023 [-0.040, -0.007]), so the paper should say the regression does not beat the bias-corrected first-order prediction for flip. For delete the regression and the null mean tie (0.262 vs 0.260); the rescaled first-order prediction is worse.
  > 
  > **C2 check** (`random_vs_formula.csv`): in z in [1,8] random deletion reversed none of the sampled pairs in any draw, and the formula gives at most 1e-9 there, so they agree only trivially; the agreement at low z is in the synthetic P_flip check (`synthetic_calibration.csv`, RMSE 0.0099). Where random does not reach q, f_q/f_adv is a lower bound: median about 600 (crowd), 23 (expert), 34 (sports) at q = 16%. Word C2 as a lower bound above z ~ 2.
  > 
  > **Positive control**: 6 jobs running (Arena-55k with blocks of 20 as clusters; MT-Bench human with its 80 question clusters). I will report the smallest size detected beyond +-0.15 per departure and graph, or "not reached", when they end. Until then C4 should say the control is pending. REPRODUCE.md now carries the disclosures (synthetic control, block-of-20 clusters, 300-pair sample).
